- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.28) within 5 days, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 7–10 days.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is erratic.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
